title: From-scratch trunk + domain-contrastive pretraining + fixed retinex channel + D4 symmetry + top-K-masked decode (forced pivot, mobilenet_v3_small banned)
hypothesis: 27 rounds since champion (exp-35, 743.07 m) have tried two disjoint kinds of change: reparameterizing the DECISION mechanism (VQ codebook exp-51 2751.73m, continuous GMM exp-52 2140.32m, three dense-per-patch-consensus variants exp-47/48/49 up to 2655.65m, IRLS robust consensus exp-55 2360.39m, spatial MoE exp-50 1109.13m, retrieve-then-rerank exp-45 1213.14m, factorized row/col axes exp-46 1e9, coordinate-generated field exp-39 1103.28m, coarse-to-fine exp-40 1011.58m) and reparameterizing the TRUNK/descriptor while leaving the decision mechanism alone or nearly alone. Every single decision-mechanism alternative to plain grid-classification-field-plus-soft-argmax has landed 1.5-3.7x worse than champion -- eight-plus independent measurements is enough to treat that family as refuted, not a shape still worth reaching into. Trunk-side changes tell a different story: exp-42 (domain-native contrastive self-supervised pretraining of a from-scratch trunk, decode/gate/field left completely untouched) reached 846.42 m, the single closest result in the entire post-champion history -- and exp-60 (a fixed, non-learned illumination-invariant retinex input channel + from-scratch trunk + cross-lighting consistency loss, gate deleted, decode otherwise untouched) reached 963.42 m, the best result of any FULLY pivot-compliant design (every non-frozen stage genuinely changed) measured so far. These are the two best post-champion results in the whole history and they attack the same thing from two different, non-overlapping angles -- what the trunk represents -- rather than how the field commits to an answer. They have never been combined, and neither has ever been tested inside a design that also legitimately rebuilds gate/ensemble/decode/confidence, which this round's compliance rule requires. Two more recent attempts at trunk swaps (exp-61 int8-quantization-freed from-scratch trunk, exp-62 SqueezeNet1.1 Fire trunk + FiLM + D4 + adaptive-beta decode) never actually trained -- both crashed on the GPU across all four areas identically before a single epoch completed, an infrastructure failure, not a measurement -- so they neither support nor refute anything, and this design deliberately keeps memory/compute modest (narrow from-scratch trunk, D4 without a wide pretrained trunk stacked under it, no learned per-example adaptive-beta MLP) specifically to avoid repeating whatever tipped those two rounds over an edge. Dispatcher/specialist-split designs (exp-30, 46, 59) have also uniformly lost, one catastrophically (exp-59, 2134.12 m) -- that family is not revisited here.
method: model/model.py: delete `from torchvision.models import mobilenet_v3_small`, `PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH`, `_build_pretrained_trunk`, `IMAGENET_MEAN`/`IMAGENET_STD` buffers, `dark_logits`, and `gate`. Replace the trunk with a small from-scratch conv stack (~150-200k params, stride 16, 48 output channels at 8x8 -- deliberately matched to champion's own 48ch/8x8 shape rather than widened, since exp-61's capacity analysis and the original pre-exp-11 from-scratch baseline (128ch, still lost to the pretrained trunk) both show raw width was never champion's advantage -- pretraining quality was) taking a 4-channel input: the raw 3-channel RGB crop plus one new fixed, non-learned illumination-invariant channel computed in forward() every pass (log-luminance minus its own large-radius fixed Gaussian blur, via a non-trainable depthwise Conv2d buffer -- no new trainable parameters, reused from CLAUDE.md SS4's ambient-vs-active-light framing and exp-60's validated approach). Extend `_c4_stack` to `_d4_stack`: the existing 4 rotations plus each one's horizontal mirror (`.flip(3)`), 8 exact-pixel views total, pure index ops, no interpolation -- keep the trunk narrow specifically so this 2x view-count increase over champion's C4 does not repeat exp-62's likely memory-driven crash (that round paired D4 with an 8x-wider 384-channel trunk; this round does not widen the trunk at all). Delete the two-expert gate/blend entirely; replace with ONE unified field head (GAP + 1x1 layout-squeeze, same shape as champion's layout-aware head) modulated by a single lightweight brightness-conditioned per-channel gain: `film_gain = nn.Linear(1, feat_ch)` (no hidden layer, ~50 params) applied as `fmap_mod = fmap * (1 + torch.tanh(film_gain(lum)).view(-1, feat_ch, 1, 1))` before the layout-squeeze and GAP -- a genuine but minimal-risk replacement for the deleted gate, not a full FiLM MLP. Change Decode: instead of sharpen-then-soft-argmax over all 1024 cells, mask to a fixed top-K=64 subset BEFORE sharpening (`topv, topi = torch.topk(logits, 64, dim=1)`; scatter into a full-size tensor filled with -inf; softmax(DECODE_BETA * masked_logits) so cells outside the top-64 get exactly zero probability) -- this directly targets the champion-failure-mode-probes diagnosis (true cell in the raw field's own top-20 of 1024 on 33-58% of crops, but top-1 only ~2%) by structurally excluding the long low-probability tail of distant lookalikes from ever contributing weighted mass to the soft-argmax centroid, rather than merely turning up the sharpening temperature on top of them. The unsharpened, UNMASKED full-field softmax is still used for the CE training loss (matching champion's exp-14 separation of 'field training signal' from 'commit decode') and for one confidence feature (top-64 raw mass fraction, a diagnostic of how concentrated the raw field already was before masking). Rebuild the confidence head over [averaged GAP descriptor, sharpened-masked peak mass, sharpened-masked entropy over 64 cells, gap between masked and unmasked decode, top-64 raw mass fraction] -- the old gate-derived inputs no longer exist. Add a self-supervised domain-contrastive pretraining routine (module-level function, called from train.py before fine-tuning): for a batch of sampled locations, load the SAME crop under two different randomly chosen lighting buckets (both already available via train.py's `_load_bucket_img` cache), run both through the trunk + GAP only (no field head), and apply a standard InfoNCE/SimCLR loss pulling the two lighting-views' GAP descriptors of the SAME location together and different locations' descriptors apart within the batch -- this is the exact recipe that produced exp-42's 846.42 m result, now applied to the new 4-channel (RGB+retinex) input. model/train.py: add a `pretrain_contrastive(model, area, meta, crops, renders_dir, data_dir, rng, device, steps=600)` function using the InfoNCE loss above, called once before the existing epoch loop in `train_area` (modest step count so four areas still finish in reasonable wall-time -- this phase only runs the trunk+GAP, not the full D4 ensemble or field head, so it is cheap per step). The existing fine-tuning loop (confusability-weighted sampler, cosine LR schedule, two-tier trunk/head LR split via `model.features.parameters()`, `calibrate_conf_shift`) is otherwise unchanged and must keep working against the new model unmodified -- only the `info['init']` string changes to describe the new strategy. `export_onnx` and `estimate_position`'s ONNX input/output contract (1x3x128x128 float32 in, [[u,v,conf]] out -- the retinex channel is computed INSIDE forward() from the 3-channel input, never added to the external contract) are unchanged.
expected_outcome: exp-42 alone (contrastive pretraining, decode/gate/field fully unchanged) reached 846.42 m (+14% vs champion); exp-60 alone (retinex channel, gate deleted, decode unchanged) reached 963.42 m (+30%). If these two independent trunk-quality levers are genuinely complementary rather than redundant, and the required additional changes (D4, top-K-masked decode, lightweight brightness gain) are neutral-to-mildly-helpful rather than harmful -- unlike every decision-mechanism reparameterization tried so far, all of which cost 1.5-3.7x -- this should land materially better than exp-60's 963.42 m, plausibly in the 650-950 m range, with a real chance of matching or beating champion's 743.07 m if the combination is synergistic. A result still above ~1000 m despite clean, uncrashed training on all four areas would be a strong new finding: it would mean neither of the two best trunk-side levers in the entire history generalizes when the decode/gate around it is also genuinely rebuilt, and future rounds should stop iterating the trunk-descriptor axis (already the best-explored axis by result quality) and interrogate training-data scale or accept the current worst-case as the practical ceiling for this design family. A crash identical in shape to exp-61/62 (all four areas fail on the GPU before any epoch prints) would indicate the infra issue is not specific to those two designs' particular width/ensemble choices and needs investigation at the loop/Modal level before the next design attempt, not another architecture rethink.
init_strategy: from-scratch (self-supervised domain-contrastive pretraining phase on the trunk before task fine-tuning; no external pretrained weights)
eli5: The last 27 attempts to beat the champion split into two piles: ones that changed HOW the model reads out its final answer from its internal map of guesses (all of them made things worse, sometimes much worse), and ones that changed WHAT the model's 'eyes' actually notice about the photo (the two best results in the whole project's history both came from this second pile). This round combines, for the first time, the two best 'better eyes' ideas that were only ever tried separately: first, the eyes get a two-part warm-up where they practice matching the SAME spot photographed under two different lighting conditions before they ever try to guess coordinates, so they learn to see past lighting changes on their own; second, every photo also gets a extra 'brightness contrast' sketch layered on top that stays roughly the same for a given spot regardless of what time of day it is, handing the eyes a shortcut to the same lesson. On top of that, since this round isn't allowed to reuse the champion's borrowed eyes at all, the two rival 'day expert / night expert' sub-brains are replaced with one brain that just gently retunes itself based on brightness, the model now also checks the mirror image of each rotated view (aerial photos really do look the same flipped), and instead of scanning its whole 1,024-cell guess-map when committing to an answer, it first throws out everything except its top 64 most-likely guesses so far-off lookalike spots can't quietly tug the final answer toward them.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px aerial crop, one of 6 simulated lighting conditions

stages.name: Illumination-invariant channel
stages.detail: a fixed, non-learned math transform computed from the raw photo every pass: how bright each patch is compared to its own broad neighborhood average — a sketch that stays roughly the same across all 6 lighting conditions for the same physical spot — stacked onto the raw color photo before anything else happens

stages.name: Symmetry ensemble
stages.detail: the crop now travels through the trunk in all 8 exact pixel arrangements of the square's full symmetry group — the previous 4 rotations, plus their mirror images, since an aerial view really is left-right symmetric — and the 8 resulting readings are averaged

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: a brand-new, never-pretrained small conv stack (matched in width to the old borrowed eyes, not wider), reading the color photo plus the new invariant sketch together — warmed up first by a practice round of matching the same spot's photo under two different lighting conditions, before ever seeing a coordinate label

stages.name: Location field
stages.detail: the old two rival 'day expert / night expert' sub-brains and their vote-blending gate are gone; one unified scorer reads the descriptor and produces the map-cell heat map, gently retuning its own sensitivity based on how bright the photo is

stages.name: Decode
stages.detail: before committing to an answer, the map's 1,024 guesses are first cut down to just the top 64 most-likely spots (everything else is thrown out, not just faded) — then the heat map's contrast is turned up as before and the answer is the balance point of what's left, so a far-off lookalike outside the top 64 can no longer tug the final answer toward it at all

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: recomputed from the new descriptor plus the shape of the top-64-only heat map (how sharp it is, and how much of the original map's certainty survived the cut) — same 'no fix' abstention idea, same tuned bar and per-bucket floor

stages.name: Training data
stages.detail: each pretraining step now also loads, for the same sampled spot, two different lighting-condition photos side by side — used only for the new warm-up round below; the confusability-weighted draw for the main training pass is unchanged

stages.name: Training procedure
stages.detail: a new, short warm-up phase runs before the usual training loop: the eyes alone (no map-guessing yet) practice recognizing that two different-lighting photos of the same spot should look alike internally, and different spots should look different; the usual training loop then runs afterward, otherwise unchanged in length

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: the warm-up phase is graded by a 'pull matching-spot photos together, push different-spot photos apart' signal; the main training phase keeps the usual grading (reward probability near the true spot) exactly as before

implementation_brief:
model/model.py: (1) Remove `from torchvision.models import mobilenet_v3_small`, `PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH`, `_build_pretrained_trunk`, `IMAGENET_MEAN`, `IMAGENET_STD`, and the `norm_mean`/`norm_std` buffers plus their use in forward(). (2) Add a from-scratch trunk builder, e.g. `_build_scratch_trunk()` returning an `nn.Sequential` of 5 conv blocks (Conv2d+BatchNorm2d+ReLU) taking 4 input channels, stride pattern reducing 128x128 -> 8x8 (four stride-2 blocks plus one stride-1 refinement), channel progression roughly 4->24->40->48->48, ending at 48 channels to match champion's downstream shapes almost exactly (minimizes ONNX-size risk and keeps the 'width was never the advantage' framing honest) -- verify with a dummy forward pass that output is [N,48,8,8]. (3) Add a non-trainable retinex buffer: `retinex_kernel` a [1,1,K,K] fixed 2D Gaussian (K=31, sigma~8px), built once in `__init__` via `torch.exp(-(dx**2+dy**2)/(2*sigma**2))` normalized to sum 1, registered with `register_buffer`. In forward(), compute `lum = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1/255)`; `blur = F.conv2d(lum, self.retinex_kernel, padding=15).clamp_min(1/255)`; `retinex = torch.log(lum) - torch.log(blur)`; `x4ch = torch.cat([x, retinex], dim=1)` -- do this INSIDE forward() on the raw [0,1] input, before `_d4_stack`, so the ONNX contract stays a plain 1x3x128x128 float input (the 4th channel is derived internally, never part of the external I/O contract). (4) Rename `_c4_stack` to `_d4_stack`: build the 4 existing rotations, then append each one's `.flip(3)` (horizontal mirror), `torch.cat` on dim 0 for 8N total views -- update every place that assumed 4 views (the `.reshape(4, n, -1).mean(dim=0)` calls in forward() become `.reshape(8, n, -1).mean(dim=0)`, and `lum4 = lum.repeat(4, 1)` becomes `lum8 = lum.repeat(8, 1)` -- lum is computed from the raw un-stacked x before D4 expansion, exactly like champion). (5) Delete `dark_logits` and `gate`. Add `self.film_gain = nn.Linear(1, feat_ch)` (feat_ch=48). In forward(), after computing `fmap = self.features(x4ch_d4stacked)` (the D4-stacked 4-channel input through the new trunk), compute `gain8 = torch.tanh(self.film_gain(lum8))`; `fmap_mod = fmap * (1 + gain8).view(-1, feat_ch, 1, 1)`; feed `fmap_mod` into the existing `layout_squeeze` (Conv2d(48,8,1), unchanged shape) and into GAP (`fmap_mod.mean(dim=(2,3))`). Concatenate flattened layout code + GAP into the single `loc_logits = nn.Linear(feat_ch + layout_ch*fmap_hw*fmap_hw, GRID_K*GRID_K)` exactly as champion's old bright-head shape (do NOT rebuild dark_logits or a gate anywhere) -- average `loc_logits` output over the 8 D4 views (`.reshape(8, n, -1).mean(dim=0)`), same pattern as champion's C4 average. (6) Decode: keep computing `p1 = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)` (unsharpened, D4-averaged, full 1024-way -- used for CE training loss, unchanged) and `u1,v1` from it for the confidence gap feature, exactly like champion. For the COMMIT decode, add top-K masking BEFORE sharpening: `K=64`; `topv, topi = torch.topk(logits, K, dim=1)`; `masked = torch.full_like(logits, float('-inf'))`; `masked.scatter_(1, topi, topv)`; `p = torch.softmax(DECODE_BETA * masked, dim=1)` (cells outside the top-K get exactly 0 probability after softmax of -inf); decode `(u,v)` from this `p` exactly as champion did (`(p*cell_u).sum(...)` etc). This `p` is what `coord_loss` trains against via `pred[:, :2]`, same as champion. (7) Confidence: `conf_head = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(feat_ch + 4, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32, 1))` reading `[f.detach() (48-d D4-averaged GAP-after-gain), peak, ent, gap, topk_mass]` where `peak`/`ent` are computed on the NEW masked-and-sharpened `p` exactly like champion computed them on its old `p`, `gap` is the same `sqrt((u-u1)**2+(v-v1)**2+eps)` as champion, and `topk_mass = p1.detach().gather(1, topi).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)` (the fraction of the RAW unsharpened field's probability mass that fell inside the eventual top-K -- a genuinely new diagnostic feature, detached, no gradient to the trunk). Keep `conf_shift` buffer and the `sigmoid(z - conf_shift)` output so train.py's `calibrate_conf_shift` needs zero changes. (8) `loss_fn` keeps its exact current shape (CE of the FULL unmasked `logits` against the Gaussian-smoothed target, `coord_loss` on `pred[:,:2]` which now reflects the top-K-masked decode, `conf_loss` BCE) -- no code change needed there, it already reads `pred`/`logits` generically. (9) Add a module-level `def contrastive_pretrain_step(model, x_view_a, x_view_b, temperature=0.1) -> torch.Tensor` computing GAP descriptors for both views through `model.features` (NOT the full D4/field pipeline -- just the raw trunk on the two single-view 4-channel inputs each, no D4 expansion needed here since this phase only needs a location-consistent descriptor, not a heading-invariant one) and returning a standard batch-level InfoNCE loss (cosine similarity matrix over the batch's `2*B` descriptors, positives = same-location pairs, all others in-batch = negatives, cross-entropy over the similarity rows) -- this function lives in model.py since it operates on model internals, imported into train.py.

model/train.py: add `pretrain_contrastive(model, area, meta, crops, renders_dir, data_dir, rng, device, steps=600, batch_size=64)`: for each step, sample `batch_size` locations via `rng.choice(len(crops), ...)`, pick two DIFFERENT lighting buckets per step (`rng.choice(list(LIGHTING_BUCKETS), size=2, replace=False)`), load both bucket images via the existing `_load_bucket_img` cache, extract the same crops (`extract_crop`, same cx/cy, independently random headings per view -- heading need not match between the two views, only location does) for each bucket, run `contrastive_pretrain_step` from model.py, backprop only through `model.features.parameters()` and `model.film_gain.parameters()` at the head LR (1e-3) using a fresh small Adam optimizer scoped to this phase only. Call this once at the start of `train_area`, right after `model = build_model().to(device)` and before the existing `opt = torch.optim.Adam(...)` / epoch loop -- keep step count modest (600 steps default) so all four areas still finish in reasonable wall-time; log the final contrastive loss value into the returned `info` dict as `contrastive_pretrain_final_loss`. Update `info['init']` to `'from-scratch (domain-contrastive self-supervised pretrain, 600 steps, RGB+retinex input, no external weights)'`. Everything else (`compute_cell_weights`, `sample_epoch`, `prepare_realizations`, `calibrate_conf_shift`, the trunk/head LR split via `model.features.parameters()`, `EPOCH_MULT`/cosine schedule) is untouched and must keep working against the new model unmodified.

Before declaring done: verify the model builds and a dummy forward pass on random [1,3,128,128] input returns a [1,3] tensor with no shape errors; verify `export_onnx` runs and the resulting file is comfortably under 4 MiB (projected ~2.6-3.0 MiB -- narrower than champion's 2.94 MiB since the dark_logits+gate removal roughly offsets the new trunk/film_gain/retinex-kernel-buffer additions, which are all small); verify an untrained (freshly initialized, no contrastive pretrain run) forward pass still decodes near the map center for a few random crops -- the bounded-downside sanity check every kept experiment since exp-14 has preserved; verify the retinex buffer's Gaussian kernel sums to 1.0 and produces no NaN/Inf on an all-black or all-white dummy crop (clamp_min guards above should already prevent this, but confirm).
